title: Effects of manipulated density of the wolf spider, Pardosa astrigera (Araneae: Lycosidae), on pest populations and cabbage yield: a field enclosure experiment
location: National Research Institute of Vegetables, Ornamental Plants and Tea (NARO), Ano, Mie Prefecture, Japan
design: RBD with 3 blocks; 2x2 m enclosed plots with transparent acrylic resin fences (45 cm tall); 3 treatments: spider-addition (P. astrigera augmented), spider-removal (P. astrigera removed via pitfall traps), open reference (unfenced, natural colonization); 3 replicates per treatment; straw mulch applied in enclosed plots only. Spring experiment (cultivar Kinkei 201, planted 21 Apr 1995, harvested mid-Jul 1995) and autumn experiment (cultivar YR-Nodoka, planted 26 Sep 1995, harvested mid-Jan 1996).
notes: This is an ADDITION experiment: wolf spiders were augmented in treatment plots and removed from control plots. Both arms are enclosed and manipulated; open reference plots were excluded from statistical analysis. Spring: 25 spiders/m2 released (100 per 4 m2 plot). Autumn: ~50 spiders/m2 released (193-211 per plot). Yield was heads+outer leaves in spring but heads only in autumn, so yield magnitudes not directly comparable across seasons. Despite significant pest suppression (P. xylostella in spring, M. persicae in autumn), yield did not significantly increase in either experiment. Statistical analyses used repeated-measures ANOVA for pest density and t-test for yield. Open-reference plots excluded from analyses due to differing conditions (no straw mulch, different weed management, no enclosure).

observations.treatment_description: spider-addition enclosures: P. astrigera augmented at 25 individuals/m2 (100 per 4 m2 plot), straw mulch applied
observations.control_description: spider-removal enclosures: P. astrigera removed via pitfall traps throughout experiment, straw mulch applied

figure_read.structure: Two groups on x-axis (Spring, Autumn); 3 bars per group: hatched=Spider-addition, gray=Spider-removal, white=Open-reference; y-axis 'Weight / plant (g)'; ticks at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600; spacing 200; linear; caption states error bars are SE. t-test results printed on figure: Spring t=2.18 df=4 p=0.095; Autumn t=1.13 df=4 p=0.32.
figure_read.evidence_note: Fig 3 p6; Spring hatched bar (spider-addition); bar top sits about 75% between 1200 and 1400 ticks (~1350 g); error bar cap extends to ~1450, SE ~100. Control (spider-removal gray bar): ~1150 g, SE ~100. Direction: spider-addition > spider-removal, as expected for predator augmentation, but p=0.095 (not significant at alpha=0.05).

observations.treatment_description: spider-addition enclosures: P. astrigera augmented at ~50 individuals/m2 (193-211 per plot, all immatures ≤5 mm), straw mulch applied
observations.control_description: spider-removal enclosures: P. astrigera removed via pitfall traps throughout experiment, straw mulch applied

figure_read.evidence_note: Fig 3 p6; Autumn hatched bar (spider-addition); bar top sits about 25% between 400 and 600 ticks (~450 g); error bar cap ~530, SE ~80. Control (spider-removal gray bar): ~390 g, SE ~60. Direction: spider-addition slightly > spider-removal, as expected, but p=0.32 (not significant).

observations.unit: individuals/plant (P. xylostella larvae+pupae, late June count)
observations.data_source: text, Results section p5 (PDF page 5); values stated: '63 vs 120 individuals/plant in late June, Fig. 1a'
observations.treatment_description: spider-addition enclosures with P. astrigera at 25/m2
observations.control_description: spider-removal enclosures with P. astrigera removed
observations.notes: Text states 'the herbivore density in the spider-addition plots was suppressed to nearly half the value of the spider-removal plots (e.g., 63 vs 120 individuals/plant in late June)'. Repeated-measures ANOVA treatment×time interaction: F=23.45, p<0.001 (Table 1). Variance (SD) shown in Fig. 1a error bars but not numerically reported for this specific date. Direction: addition reduces pest abundance as expected.

observations.unit: individuals/plant (M. persicae adults+nymphs, late November count)
observations.data_source: text, Results section p5 (PDF page 5); values stated: '33 vs 816 individuals/plant in late November, Fig. 1b'
observations.treatment_description: spider-addition enclosures with P. astrigera at ~50/m2
observations.control_description: spider-removal enclosures with P. astrigera removed
observations.notes: Text states 'The abundance of M. persicae in the spider-addition plots was strongly suppressed and kept at low densities throughout the autumn experiment (e.g., 33 vs 816 individuals/plant in late November)'. Repeated-measures ANOVA treatment×time interaction: F=18.68, p=0.008 (Table 1). Variance (SD) shown in Fig. 1b error bars (caption says ±SD) but not numerically reported for this date. Direction: addition dramatically reduces aphid abundance as expected.
